caseno: Writ Petition Nos. 9391 of 2011 with 9414 of 2011.
lawyer:
Fida M Kamal with Md Oziullah, and Md Iqbal Kabir, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Mahbubey Alam, Attorney-General with Md Al-Amin Sarker, Deputy Attorney-General and Dr Shahdeen Malik with Zahirul Alam Babor and Manjurul Ahsan—For the Respondents.
parties:
Nurul Imran Chisty and others ------- Petitioner (in WP No. 9391 of 2011)
vs
State and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment: 4. The short facts, as stated in the writ petitions, for disposal of the Rules are that the petitioners in both the writ petitions are reputed Domestic and International Courier Service Operators in Bangladesh having been engaged in their respective businesses since 1983 upon obtaining valid trade license and necessary permission from the concerned authorities and are paying VAT, Income Tax and other charges to the Government. It is the petitioners' claim that they generate a substantial amount of the revenue earned by the Courier and Express Industry as a whole in Bangladesh. It is stated that the petitioners are, per force, contractually affiliated to various overseas Agencies, Franchisee Service Providers, Contractors and Joint Ventures as they do not possess their own international network in the relevant field. It is further stated that before enactment of the Post Office (Amendment) Act 2010, the mailing operators and courier service providers were regulated by the following laws, namely, the Post Office Act 1898, the Customs Act 1969, the Value Added Tax Act 1991, the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 and Import and Export Control Act, 1950. It is stated that by amendment to the Post Office Act 1898 on 28-1-2010 and framing Rules there under, namely, (মেইলিং অপারেটর ও কুরিয়ার সার্ভিস বিধিমালা, ২০১১) the Postal Department was relieved from the obligation to pay any compensation and demurrage against loss, wrong delivery and delay in delivery whereas penalties and compensatory fines were imposed on the petitioners for the commission of the said actions, which is a clear violation of Article 27 of the Constitution. It is further stated that the Rules, insofar as they relate to payment of compensations to foreign companies in Bangladesh and their Agencies, are inconsistent with the Rules and Regulation framed by the World Trade Organization (WTO) and, there-fore, implementation of the Rules, as has been framed by the respondents, requires consent of, and ratification by, the principals of foreign companies operating in Bangladesh and their governments. It is further stated that the Post Office Act, 1898 has been amended by Parliament in 2010 incorporating certain new provisions to regulate universal postal service and for international communication by the National Public Postal operation. Section 4B of the said Act empowers the concerned authority to issue license to the mailing operators and courier service providers. The licensing authority has been constituted under section 4C of the said Act and by virtue of the said section, power has conferred upon the Government to frame Rules for the purposes, amongst others, to determine appropriate License fees and other charges and commissions for operating mailing and courier services. The amended law has authorised the licensing committee to regulate the aforesaid financial matters. The Rules framed thereunder, insofar as they relate to the said matters, are contrary to the amended law and beyond jurisdiction and hence illegal and void. It is further stated that the Postal Department of the Government of Bangladesh is a direct competitor of the petitioners andboth parties are engaged in the same business. But while inserting the provision in the Post Office Act, 1898 by the amendment of the Act in 2010, imposing penalty upon the petitioners, no provision has been laid down in the amended Act of 2010 or in the Rules of 2011 for imposing similar penalty upon the Postal Department. It is alleged that the government has thus given special privilege to the Postal Department by exempting them from liability. It is further stated that after enactment of the Post Office (Amendment) Act 2010, Secretary of the Ministry of Post and Telecommunication held a meeting on 14th of August, 2010 regarding the purpose of the said amendment as well as the necessity and purpose of framing proposed Rules thereunder to carry out the purpose of the parent law. The meeting was attended by the representatives from the petitioners and some officials from the Ministry of Post and Tele-communication. In the meeting the following resolutions were adopted: (s) "International Air Express Association of Bangladesh এবং Courier Service Association of Bangladesh এর পক্ষ হতে ১ (এক) সপ্তাহের মধ্য মেইলিং অপারেটর ও কুরিয়ার সার্ভিস বিধিমালা ২০১১’ এর সার সংক্ষেপের উপর স্ব স্ব এসোসিয়েশনের মতামত মন্ত্রনালয়ে প্রেরণ করবে। (খ) কুরিয়ার প্রতিষ্ঠানের নিকট হতে বিধিমালার উপর মতামত প্রাপ্তির পর বিধিমালা প্রণয়ণের জন্য গঠিত কমিটি পুনরায় সভা আহ্বান করবে। It is stated that as per the resolution of the meeting the petitioners submitted their recommendation to the respondents on 19-9-2010 which was received by the respondent No.2 on 20-9-2010 but, in total disregard to the petitioners' suggestions, respondent No. 1 published (মেইলিং অপারেটর ও কুরিয়ার সার্ভিস বিধিমালা, ২০১১)  in the Official Gazette on 13-9-2011 vide SRO No.288- Ain/2011. The petitioners found the impugned Rules to be ultra vires of Articles 27, 31 and 40 of the Constitution and inconsistent and repugnant to sections 4C and 58 of the Post Office Act, 1898 which prompted the petitioners to file the instant writ petitions. Hence these Rules.
